is it possible to install directly to hard drive from a USB stick, or is it essential?

Your question makes no sense. From the USB stick you install to the hard drive in the standard use case.

You can use Linux Mint Cinnamon 17.2 from a USB stick at first. If you like it, you can install it to the hard disk from the stick, but you don't have to - you can keep using the stick.

Does that answer your question?

If you're new to Linux, I recommend letting the installer make partition choices for you. Nothing worse than guessing and make a required partition a too-small fixed size (OS will crash or freeze when the partition is full). While there are some optimization gains from manually creating partitions, this is for experienced users and the gains aren't so significant you should try to do the same. Hey, enjoy Linux!

You can boot the OS from the USB stick. This means no permanent files are written to your hard drive. The OS is launched from the USB stick.

If you wish to install a "permanent" copy where the OS just starts when your power on your computer, that is possible and simple also. Just get the installer files and put them on a USB stick. Then, boot from your USB stick the next time you boot up your computer. You should see a graphical installer and you will be able to partition your computer's hard drive right in Mint's graphical installer.

You can quickly google something like "install linux mint" and you will see a good amount of information about setting up the installer and partitioning your hard drive correctly.

If done right, your whole installation will only take your like 15 minutes. Good luck!
